lines.trans: Let me speak honestly—I think you are a good person, Ms. Cindy, yet it seems you do not view yourself that way.
And so at some point, I wonder if you ended up performing even your sincere feelings like an act.
Are you giving me your answer right now to what I asked you that night?
Producer Ra Joon-mo once told me that since this is reality variety, all I need to do is comfortably show my true self.
Except—what even is my true self as I am? I honestly do not know.
Just like you said, when I neither think of myself as a good person nor love myself nor even know myself…
Who on earth would think well of me—who would ever like me, who would ever understand me?
I will consider your answer heard loud and clear, Producer—goodbye.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: refers to a previously mentioned or specific day

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
I don't have time that day.

examples.text: 뭘 하려고 그러지 말고 그냥 있는 그대로 보여 주면 되거든요.
examples.trans: Don't try to put anything on, just show yourself as you really are.

examples.text: 있는 그대로, 내 모습 그대로? 알겠어요.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So how is it?
So I went.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: 답이 없다 ('there is no answer') is a common idiom meaning a situation is hopeless.

examples.trans: There's really no answer to this problem.
I found the answer to the question.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (대답을).

examples.text: 뭐야, 왜 대답을 못 해? 갑자기 왜 선배님이 선배가 됐지?
examples.trans: What is it, why can you not answer? How did honored Senior suddenly turn into plain Senior?

examples.text: 당연하지, 좋지! 우리 술 먹을 때 원래 이러고 놀아, 무조건 대답을 당연하지라고 해야 되는 거야.
examples.trans: Of course, I love it! We always play this when drinking—no matter what, you have to answer "Of course"!

meanings.note: Used as past adnominal (되어버린).
